name: CRT collapse to line

source.description: An inspected brand reel (batch 1, 2026-11-26) squashes a word vertically into a bright horizontal line, like a tube television switching off, and the line carries into the next frame.

technique: The frame or a word collapses vertically into a thin bright line (scaleY to almost zero, slight horizontal stretch, brightness up); the line holds or extends and becomes a rule, a connector or the next element. Reversed, the line opens into a new frame.
purpose: A fast, graphic exit that leaves a continuity element (the line) for the next scene.
visual_behaviour: Word squashes to a line in 0.1-0.15 s with vertical motion blur; a thin line remains, then extends or fades.
mechanics: scaleY 1 -> 0.02 with power3.in over 0.12 s, scaleX 1 -> 1.08, filter brightness 1 -> 1.6 and a 2-4 px vertical blur during the squash; the remaining line is a separate 1-2 px rule that takes over (extend scaleX or fade). transform-origin at the vertical centre.

parameters.name: line
parameters.description: What the line becomes: rule, connector, fade

use_cases: exit of a headline into a divider
failure_modes: Too slow reads as a squash-and-stretch gag, not a power-off
Without the brightness lift it looks like a scale bug

implementation.approach: GSAP fromTo on the word or scene container (scaleY, scaleX, filter) then hand off to a separately drawn rule; reverse for an 'on'.

provenance.observed: After an inversion cut the word squashes vertically with blur into a thin bright line (3.42-3.49 s) that remains as a rule in the next frame.
Reversed: a one-pixel line thickens (1.62-1.68 s) and opens vertically into a full orange frame by 1.75 s (0.13 s).
Reverse (power-on) variant: a pulsing dot vanishes, a hairline grows across the frame (3.7-4.3 s), opens into a band (4.4 s) and then into the full interface frame (4.5-4.8 s).
The word card collapses into a horizontal line and then a dot (4.54-4.64 s); a ring opens on grey (4.67-4.74 s).

licensing_notes: Technique only, learned from user-supplied references (inspiration-only, rights unknown).
